title: Finite-time breakdown for Navier–Stokes and Euler
abstract: Formalizes forced three-dimensional Navier–Stokes breakdown on Euclidean space and the periodic torus for every positive viscosity, and finite-time singularity formation for unforced Euler from smooth, compactly supported, divergence-free initial data. The Euler result specifies maximal Sobolev lifespan, divergence of the velocity C¹ norm, and divergence of the time integral of the vorticity norm.

informal.NavierStokes.Comparator.navier_stokes_br: For every positive viscosity, there are smooth divergence-free initial data and smooth forcing on ℝ³, with the prescribed spatial and temporal decay, admitting no global smooth Navier–Stokes solution with uniformly bounded kinetic energy.

For every positive viscosity, there are smooth periodic divergence-free initial data and smooth periodic forcing with the prescribed temporal decay, admitting no global smooth periodic Navier–Stokes solution.
informal.Euler.euler_breakdown_R3: There exist smooth divergence-free initial data on ℝ³ whose spatial derivatives decay faster than every polynomial and which admit no global smooth unforced Euler solution with uniformly bounded kinetic energy.
informal.Euler.exists_compact_smooth_euler_singul: There exist nonzero smooth compactly supported divergence-free initial data, a maximal time 0 < Tstar ≤ 1, and an unforced Euler solution on [0, Tstar) in the all-order Sobolev class with bounded kinetic energy. Smooth Sobolev solutions on [0, T] exist exactly when T < Tstar. The velocity C¹ norm has infinite left limsup at Tstar, and the time integral of the spatial supremum of the vorticity norm diverges.
